newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market calm, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market calm, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. feedlot cattle markets in the central and southern Plains were quiet, with no sales reported near midday on Tuesday, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were mostly at $63.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00. There was one report of a bid at $63.50 in the Texas Panhandle that also was passed, sources there said.
"A bid at $64.00 would buy some cattle, but I don't think packers will buy anything today," a Panhandle area source said. "They have enough cattle to get into Thursday."
Just as packer buyers appeared willing to wait another day before buying cattle, several cattle feeders said owners also were willing to wait amid ideas firm beef prices would support cattle prices.

However, outlooks for beef prices were shaky amid ideas last week's large slaughter would replenish tight stocks and that retailers were winding up purchases for Independence Day beef features, market sources said.
Cattle slaughter last week was estimated at 720,000 head, up 1.8 percent from the previous week at 707,000, USDA statistics showed.

Beef prices at midday Tuesday were quoted down $0.29 to $0.46 per cwt, with 165 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said. Closing beef prices Monday had been quoted higher, leading some market watchers to believe beef prices possibly had not topped out seasonally, as some expected late last week.
